messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered - multiple containers in inference-prod/inference-a are crashlooping with SIGSEGV in runtime/engine (vLLM kernel). Observed ~4 nodes flapping. 502/503 upstream errors hitting 10% of requests. Root ts 1887654321

jordan: I'm on it - paging oncall. jordan (oncall) taking lead. Which customers are showing errors in the dashboard?

ops-bot: Impacted routes: /v1/generate (primary). Customers with increased error rate: acme-ads, edu-ai (approx 1.2% and 0.6% of total error volume respectively). Autoscaler is bouncing some pods.

jordan: ok. first quick mitigation: cordon affected nodes and scale down pool to avoid new pods landing there. lee, can you cordon 3 nodes in inference-a and scale down the k8s replica count by 30%?

lee: on it. cordoning nodes n-inf-a-03 n-inf-a-07 n-inf-a-11

lee: commands run:
```
kubectl cordon n-inf-a-03
kubectl cordon n-inf-a-07
kubectl cordon n-inf-a-11
kubectl -n inference scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=14
```
Nodes cordoned and replicas scaled down. New pods are being scheduled to other pools.

maria: @jordan quick context: we deployed runtime-engine v2.3.7 yesterday with a fused attention kernel for some LLMs. There were perf wins but we saw an internal test with rare pointer handling on long contexts. Not widespread.

sana: we have fallback routing to non-fused runtime variant, can we flip traffic for the affected model family to the safe variant?

jordan: yes, do that now. sana, route model-family "ours-13b" to runtime:v2.3.6-safe. Also enable 429-based backoff for heavy clients.

sana: done. Routing rule applied:
```
route set --model-family=ours-13b --target=runtime:v2.3.6-safe --weight=100
```
Traffic change effective within 20s.

jordan: logs from one crashed pod attached in-line:
```
[2029-06-17T14:12:04Z] runtime-engine[pid:1] SIGSEGV at 0x0 ip=0x7f9c4a12ef40
#0  0x7f9c4a12ef40 in fused_attention::process_chunk() +0x120
#1  0x7f9c4a130abc in vllm::forward() +0x3c
#2  0x7f9c4a11a9fd in main_loop() +0x1a4
```
Possible null-deref in fused_attention when KV cache chunking boundary occurs.

maria: can you get a core dump and dmesg from the node? maybe a memory corruption or underrun from the CUDA driver.

lee: dmesg shows repeated:
```
[987654.321] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: GPU fault: Xid 31, Ch 00000001, intr 10000000
[987654.322] kernel: segfault at 0 ip 00007f9c4a12ef40 sp 00007fffb1c3c8c0 error 4
```
Also NVML reports GPU reset on the node after the crash.

maria: Xid 31 usually points to illegal memory access in a GPU kernel. Combined with SIGSEGV in userland, likely memory corruption crossing into host pointers or a bad pointer math in fused kernel. Need reproducer.

jordan: mitigation status: cordoned nodes, traffic routed to safe runtime, replicas scaled down. Error rate dropped from 10% to 0.8% within 2 mins. Customers acme-ads/edu-ai hit errors short-term but now recovering. Notify SRE/Customer Success.

ops-bot: Notifying #customer-alerts: Short-term error spike for acme-ads and edu-ai, routed to safe variant. Postmortem will follow.

sana: can we disable fused kernel at runtime quickly? maria, is there a runtime flag we can flip without rollback?

maria: yes, env var `RUNTIME_USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=false` will disable the new path. We can patch the deployment and rolling-restart.

jordan: let's patch and roll the runtime replicas -- but only after we confirm traffic has stabilized for affected customers. lee, hold for 2 more minutes.

lee: holding. metrics stable at 0.7% errors now. proceeding with patch.

lee:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/inference-runtime RUNTIME_USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=false
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime
```
Rollout started, 5 pods restarting in parallel.

maria: I'm pulling the crash pod image and running under gdb to get a better stack and check for allocator races. If we can reproduce locally with curated inputs we can bisect the commit.

jordan: any sign of OOMs or host OOM killer? That would indicate memory pressure rather than kernel bug.

lee: no oom_score_adj kills; node memory free is fine. GPU OOM not reported prior to segfault - this is a kernel launch fault (Xid 31) per NV driver logs.

maria: collecting core and gdb backtrace. Also grabbing /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and CUDA driver version. Attaching stack from gdb run:
```
#0 fused_attention::process_chunk
#1 vllm::forward
#2 vllm::main
#3 __libc_start_main
```
Looks very deterministic for the input sequence length ~2048 with chunk boundary at 1024.

sana: from routing metrics, ~30% of requests for the family were at 2048 context. Likely a boundary case.

jordan: good job team. Current state: rollout finishing, traffic on safe runtime, cordons in place, customers recovering. I'll escalate to oncall handoff notes and create an incident ticket for follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2029-1879. Severity P2 -> P1 because customer-facing errors briefly exceeded SLA.

jordan: oncall handoff: I'm pausing here at 15:30 UTC for handoff to night SRE. Key actions for next shift:
- collect core dumps and store in s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-2029-1879/
- run bisect on fused_attention commit range (tag v2.3.7 changeset)
- verify canary traffic to safe runtime and then re-enable fused kernel behind strict canary and longer context tests
- write postmortem: include reproducer input and suggested guardrails (input length checks, kernel bounds checks)

lee: uploaded dmesg, kube events, and pod logs to incident bucket.

maria: I'll open a PR to add an assert/guard for chunk index calc and add a unit test with long context seam cases. Also propose a runtime config to disable fused path for specific models until verified.

sana: customer success contact: pinged acme-ads and edu-ai with incident summary and remediation steps. They'll monitor for residual errors.

jordan: marking this thread resolved here. Please add any follow-ups to the INC ticket. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2029-1879 status -> mitigated. Postmortem assigned to maria. Follow-up actions assigned: SRE/Runtime/ML teams.

maria: filing PR and will include reproducer and perf impact numbers. Expect follow-up in 24-48h.

lee: leaving cordons in place until nodes are reproved and GPU driver checks done.

sana: will keep routing rule in place for 12h then test slow ramp if safe.

jordan: end of thread. Remember to attach any coredumps and gdb output to INC ticket.
